article.title: Why Writing Down the Next Step Makes Work Easier to Restart
article.why: 降低工作中斷後重新進入任務的認知成本。
article.author: OpenAI learning editor

paragraphs.en:
When a task is interrupted, the hardest part of restarting is often not the task itself. It is remembering what you were doing, why you were doing it, and what should happen next. A simple note can solve much of this problem.

Before you stop, write one clear next step. It should be an action that can be started immediately. “Continue the analysis” is vague. “Check whether the August sales drop comes from fewer customers or lower spend per customer” is much better.

This small note reduces the time needed to rebuild context. Without it, you may reopen several files, reread messages, and repeat part of your previous thinking. With it, you can move directly into action.

The note also helps when work is interrupted by meetings, urgent requests, lunch, or the end of the day. In knowledge work, these interruptions are normal. The goal is not to avoid them completely, but to leave yourself an easy restart point.

A useful next-step note can include a file name, a question to answer, or a person to contact. It does not need to be long. One sentence is often enough. If the task is complex, add one reason: “Next, compare the two segments because the total average may hide a mix change.”

This habit is also useful for teamwork. If someone else must continue your work, a visible next step makes the handover much easier. It also reduces the chance that a task stays “almost done” simply because nobody knows the next move.

Try it today. Before you close a task, write one sentence beginning with: “Next, I will…” Tomorrow, notice how quickly you can restart. The saved time may be only a few minutes each time, but across many interruptions, those minutes add up. A clear restart point also makes it easier to stop working without worrying that you will lose the thread.
paragraphs.zh: 工作被中斷後，真正耗時的往往不是任務本身，而是重新想起做到哪裡、為什麼做、下一步是什麼。離開前寫下一個具體可執行的 next step，就能降低重建脈絡的成本。
paragraphs.ja: 作業中断後に時間がかかるのは、作業そのものより文脈の再構築です。離れる前に次の具体的な行動を一文で残すと、再開時にすぐ動けます。

vocabulary.usage: A visible next step helps a handover.

phrases.explanation: 替自己留下重新開始的切入點
phrases.example: Leave yourself a clear restart point.

grammar.title: Before + clause
grammar.body: Before you close a task 表示在關閉任務前。

business.term: What is the next concrete action?
business.explanation: 把模糊工作轉為可執行下一步
business.example: Before we stop, what is the next concrete action?

business.term: I’ll leave the next step in the note.
business.explanation: 交接時說明已留下下一步
business.example: I’ll leave the next step in the note for tomorrow.

quiz.question: Why does a next-step note help?
quiz.answer: It reduces the time needed to rebuild context.
